clue.text: Graduate cuts amounts left in bank account

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate's degree
to lance is to cut open, as a surgeon does a boil

explanation.surface: A graduate trims down whatever money remains in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Balances are the sums remaining in accounts after debits and credits are reckoned.

clue.text: Fuss about daughter having lover

parts.note: a fuss is an ado, as in much ado about nothing
re means about or concerning, as in business letters
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: Parents make a fuss about their daughter's new boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a devoted lover is worshipped and cherished by that person.

clue.text: Liberal politician gets in the beer

indicators.note: the politician gets inside the beer, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat politician turns up at the pub and gets the drinks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal in the sense of generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping.

clue.text: Sharing guilt, company member needs legal support

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath the one it holds up

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: A firm's employee, an accomplice in wrongdoing, needs a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice involved in a wrongful act shares the blame for it.

clue.text: Light coming down a shaft

parts.note: a shaft of light is a ray streaming down, not a mine shaft or a spear

explanation.surface: Daylight filtering down a mine or lift shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of daylight from the sky is literally a shaft of light descending.

clue.text: Signing for course

parts.note: the hand-signal system bookmakers use at a racecourse to pass on betting odds

explanation.walkthrough: Tic-tac is the arm-waving code of British bookmakers at the races; 'course' is a racecourse, not a meal or a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookies' semaphore at a racecourse, used to signal odds between them.

clue.text: Unit for heating the small room

parts.note: taken as written
RM is the abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: Someone checks the heating settings in the small spare room.
explanation.walkthrough: A therm is a British unit of heat once used for gas bills.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heat equal to 100,000 British thermal units, used for gas supply.

clue.text: Coins lost, possibly, but they settle

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could form another word if rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone loses some coins, perhaps, but pays the bill anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlers who establish new communities in a foreign land are pioneers.

clue.text: One missing tea's been out

indicators.note: out signals that the preceding letters are disordered, as in put out of place

explanation.surface: A person is absent because they have gone out for afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fails to attend is away from where they should be.

clue.text: Cannon ball?

definitions.meaning: a ... is a rapid-firing automatic anti-aircraft gun
a fluffy woollen ball on a hat

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the spelling: a quick-firing naval gun and a woolly tuft on a bobble hat.

clue.text: Want no more, it's unnecessary

parts.note: to want is to need
less in the sense of not more

explanation.surface: Wanting nothing further, someone declares it all superfluous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncalled-for is not required at all, hence superfluous.

clue.text: Military call-up

parts.note: not conscription but the bugle signal that calls soldiers up out of bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Call-up' looks like conscription; read it as a call to get up in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning bugle signal that wakes troops at dawn.

clue.text: Industry in which men are under-employed

definitions.text: Industry in which men are under-employed

parts.words: Industry in which men are under-employed
parts.note: under-employed read as employed underground, not lacking enough work

explanation.surface: A gloomy economic report on a sector with too little work.
explanation.definitionFit: Colliery workers dig coal far beneath the surface of the earth.

clue.text: Expert carried out

definitions.meaning: skilled or highly ... in some art
achieved or completed, as a task done

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is skilful and polished; the other is completed or achieved successfully.

clue.text: Coming to river — that may be exciting

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Arriving at a river promises something thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit or escapade is by nature thrilling and risky.

clue.text: Nasty hotel, so am moving

indicators.note: moving says the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A guest leaves a dreadful hotel and declares they are moving out.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsive or detestable things are thoroughly unpleasant.

clue.text: A right pursued by one US state and another

indicators.note: pursued by puts the following state after the first two letters

parts.note: Kansas is a state in the American Midwest

explanation.surface: Someone on the right is chased from one American state into the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'another' means a second US state, following on from 'one US state'.
explanation.definitionFit: A southern American state neighbouring Oklahoma, a second state after the first named.

clue.text: Soldier intends to acquire personal wealth

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier
to mean is to intend

explanation.surface: A soldier plans to come into a fortune of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Independent income from investments or inheritance rather than earnings.

clue.text: His job is to cast waste away

definitions.meaning: a person who makes moulds or castings in a foundry

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a foundry worker making casts; the other is to rot gradually.

clue.text: Vehicle provided for those who are late

definitions.text: Vehicle provided for those who are late

parts.words: Vehicle provided for those who are late
parts.note: late in the sense of deceased, not behind time

explanation.surface: A minibus laid on for latecomers who missed the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: The funeral car carrying a coffin for the dead.

clue.text: Standard CND supporter?

definitions.meaning: a flag, as carried on a march
CND, the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, wants to ban the bomb, so a supporter is one who bans

explanation.walkthrough: CND is a British anti-nuclear campaign group whose slogan was Ban the Bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag or standard; and whimsically, one who bans, as CND supporters would ban the bomb.

clue.text: Not left straight

explanation.definitionFit: Opposite of left in direction; also direct, as in a right line or right angle.

clue.text: Made the young go off their rockers?

definitions.text: Made the young go off their rockers?

parts.words: Made the young go off their rockers?
parts.note: going off one's rocker means going mad; here children fall off rocking horses

explanation.surface: Something drove the youngsters crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown from a horse, here a nursery rocking horse.

clue.text: They spread out in all directions

definitions.text: They spread out in all directions

parts.words: They spread out in all directions
parts.note: lines from a circle's centre fanning out every way, not a crowd dispersing

explanation.surface: A crowd scatters every which way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines from the centre of a circle extend to its edge at every angle.

clue.text: Satisfied when sausage mash is set before a number

indicators.note: the anagram goes in front of the next piece
mash means crush into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Hunger is appeased by bangers and mash served before a large crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mash' rearranges SAUSAGE into ASSUAGE; D is Roman 500. 'Sausage mash' suggests the British dish bangers and mash.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeased or eased, as hunger or a craving is relieved.

clue.text: Directions taken by clergymen?

explanation.definitionFit: Commands given; and the holy ordination that priests receive on entering the ministry.

clue.text: Acquiesce when told to go

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I arrived
someone sent away has been told to go

explanation.surface: Someone gives in once they are ordered to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree or consent, going along with something.

clue.text: Revised diet distributed in rush

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the plant

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like water plant

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slimming plan is revised and handed out in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like haste but is the waterside plant; 'distributed' rearranges the diet and 'in' tucks the result into that plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited again, as a text gone over a second time.
